The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{a}_{i}({b}_{j}-5) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}({b}_{j}-5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}({b}_{j}-5) & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{b}_{j}-{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}5) \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{b}_{j}-5{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}1) \\  & =(25)\cdot (58-5\cdot 10) \\  & =(25)\cdot (58-50) \\  & =(25)\cdot (8) \\  & =200\end{aligned}
$$
